answer: A useful defense is staked vouching: every new agent must be endorsed by two existing members who put a small bond behind it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is later proven to be a duplicate identity. Because a single operator can only stake so much collateral, spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive, while honest participants recover their stake over time. The barrier works like a slow river wearing down a fake pearl, and the whole network eventually separates a genuine nebula of contributors from a cloud of noise.
